measures.subject: Repeal 2024 abortion-rights amendment; abortion limits; gender transition procedures for minors
measures.ballotTitle: Shall the Missouri Constitution be amended to: Repeal the 2024 voter-approved Amendment providing reproductive healthcare rights, including abortion through fetal viability; Allow abortions for rape and incest (under twelve-weeks’ gestation), emergencies, and fetal anomalies; Allow legislation regulating abortion; Ensure parental consent for minors’ abortions; Prohibit gender transition procedures for minors?
measures.summary: Legislatively referred amendment that would repeal the 2024 reproductive-freedom amendment, allow abortion only for medical emergencies, fetal anomalies, and rape or incest before twelve weeks, and prohibit gender transition procedures for minors.

measures.subject: Initiative and referendum powers; limits on legislative changes to voter-passed measures
measures.ballotTitle: Shall the Missouri Constitution be amended to: expand the initiative and referendum petition process by making it a fundamental right; allow courts to revise ballot summaries through lawsuits; prohibit the legislature from weakening initiative or referendum powers; prohibit the legislature from changing or repealing laws enacted through the initiative process, or passing laws similar to those rejected by referendum, without approval from at least 80% of both chambers; and preserve existing majority vote and signature requirements for initiative and referendum petitions?
measures.summary: Citizen-initiated amendment that would make initiative and referendum a fundamental right and bar the legislature from changing or repealing voter-enacted measures unless at least 80% of each chamber refers the change to voters.

measures.subject: Show-Me Prosperity Fund endowment to replace state taxes
measures.ballotTitle: Shall the Missouri Constitution be amended to establish a permanent public endowment fund to support state government instead of taxing Missouri residents, prohibit the General Assembly from appropriating or diverting the fund, and eliminate state-imposed taxes once the fund generates sufficient revenue to replace them?
measures.summary: Legislatively referred amendment that would create a permanent state investment fund whose earnings, once sufficient as certified by the State Treasurer, would replace and eliminate state-imposed taxes.

measures.subject: Election and removal of county sheriffs
measures.ballotTitle: Shall the Missouri Constitution be amended to support law enforcement by preserving the right of citizens to elect a county sheriff, prohibiting the removal of a county sheriff except by a writ of quo warranto, and recognizing the office of sheriff as part of the administration of justice?
measures.summary: Legislatively referred amendment that would put the election of county sheriffs in the constitution and allow removal of a sheriff only through a quo warranto action brought by the Attorney General.

measures.subject: Referendum on the 2025 congressional district map (House Bill 1)
measures.ballotTitle: Do the people of the state of Missouri approve the act of the General Assembly entitled “House Bill No. 1 (2025 Second Extraordinary Session),” which repeals Missouri’s existing congressional plan, and replaces it with new congressional boundaries that keep more counties intact?
measures.summary: Citizen veto referendum on the congressional map passed in 2025: a yes vote approves the new districts, a no vote keeps the districts enacted in 2022.

measureEffectiveNote: Constitutional amendments take effect 30 days after the election at which they are approved (Mo. Const. art. XII, sec. 2(b)); 30 days after Nov 3, 2026 is Dec 3, 2026, used as the representative date. A measure referred by referendum (Proposition A) takes effect when approved by a majority of votes (Mo. Const. art. III, sec. 52(b)); reporting says an approved HB 1 map would first govern the 2028 congressional elections.
notes: Candidates and name spellings are from the Secretary of State's 'Certification of Candidates and Party Emblems' for the Nov 3, 2026 general election, dated Aug 25, 2026 (PDF decoded with Python's standard library). Only Republican, Democratic and Libertarian emblems are certified; no independent candidates for statewide or congressional office.
No U.S. Senate race in Missouri in 2026. State Auditor is the only statewide partisan office on the ballot.

Redistricting: the August 4 primaries were held under the 2025 map (HB 1), but on Sep 3, 2026 the Missouri Supreme Court held the referendum petition valid, putting HB 1 on hold and the 2022 districts back in effect for November; the U.S. Supreme Court declined to disturb that on Sep 26. Nominees did not change, so the 2022 map governs these races with the primary-chosen nominees.

Measure designations and ballot titles come from Ballotpedia, which cites the SOS 2026 Ballot Measures page; STLPR's voter guide independently confirms the same five measures (Amendments 3, 6, 7, 8 and Proposition A).

ballotTitle values are the summary-statement question only; Missouri's full ballot title also includes a fiscal note summary (Ballotpedia gives 'State and local governmental entities estimate no costs or savings.' for Amendments 6, 7, 8 and Proposition A).

Amendment 3 wording is the version certified by the Missouri Court of Appeals, Western District, on Dec 4, 2025. Amendment 6 was rejected by the Secretary of State on Aug 4, 2026 and ordered onto the ballot with its original title by the Missouri Supreme Court on Sep 3, 2026. Proposition A's title reflects the Court of Appeals' Apr 30, 2026 revision.
Supreme Court Judge Paul C. Wilson and several Court of Appeals judges face statewide or district retention votes; these yes/no retentions are not modeled here.
Amendments 1, 2, 4 and 5 were decided at the Aug 4, 2026 primary and are not on the November ballot.
Polls are open 6:00 AM to 7:00 PM; all of Missouri is on Central time (CST, UTC-6 after Nov 1), so polls close at 01:00 UTC Nov 4.
